newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Lebed's new Russian party ejects anti-Semite.
newsitem.headline: Lebed's new Russian party ejects anti-Semite.

text.p: General Alexander Lebed faced an awkward moment on Saturday when a supporter of his new Russian political party serenaded him with an anti-Semitic verse in front of massed television cameras.

The tough-talking ex-paratrooper looked on stony-faced, then had the man bodily ejected from the party's inauguration ceremony after a word in his ear from world chess champion Garry Kasparov, who is a prominent Lebed supporter and half-Jewish.
The offender, dressed in combat fatigues, was identified by Russian media as Georgy Getman, chairman of an association for army officers known as Shit (The Shield).
Taking his turn signing a book of support for Lebed's new Russian Popular Republican Party, he recited a patriotic verse which concluded with a disparaging reference to Jews.
After a word from Kasparov, sitting at Lebed's right hand, the former Kremlin security chief quoted 19th century author Nikolai Gogol, saying Russia suffered from "a lot of idiots".
The man was then bundled from the room by aides.
Lebed, who hails from Cossack stock in southern Russia, where there is a long tradition of anti-Semitism, has had to deny in the past that he has anti-Jewish prejudices.

U.S. President Bill Clinton demanded an explanation from the Kremlin last year after Lebed, during his time on President Boris Yeltsin's staff, was quoted as saying Russia had three official religions -- Orthodox Christianity, Islam and Buddhism.
The country is estimated to have the world's third largest Jewish population after the United States and Israel.
